summary: S. G. F. Brandon worked in religious studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leeds (~1927–1932) and held a post at the University of Manchester (~1951–1971), where he taught Eric J. Sharpe.

S. Kuppuswami Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Brahmendra Sarasvati and Nilakanta Sastri, and at the University of Madras. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, and held professorships at Presidency College and Annamalai University.

S. M. Natesa Sastri worked in Indology. He studied at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras (~1878–1881), and served as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1883–1892).

S. N. Balagangadhara works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at National College, Bangalore, and earned his doctorate under Etienne Vermeersch at Ghent University, where he later served as Director (~1991–2017).
S. N. Krishna is an Indologist who studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor T. V. Vasudeva (attested 2026).
S. N. Savadi worked in Indology and held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.

S. S. Misra was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor and Head of the Sanskrit Department at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri worked in philosophy and Indology. He served at the University of Madras as Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and later as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942).

S. Sankaranarayanan worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as an Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1986–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

S. Srikanta Sastri worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under M. H. Krishna (~1923–1926) and held an academic post at the University of Mysore (~1926–1960).

Saba Mahmood worked in religious studies and anthropology. She studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University (PhD ~1992–1998), and held faculty posts at the University of Chicago (~2000–2004) and the University of California, Berkeley (2004–2018).

Sabine Klein-Schwind is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Harunaga Isaacson and has served as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Sabine Löhr studied Indology at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, completing her doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen. She also served as a research assistant (Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft) at the University of Hamburg.
Sabriye Tenberken works in Tibetology. She studied at the University of Bonn (~1992–1997) and founded Braille Without Borders.

Saburō Hasegawa worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929) and taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies (~1953–1957) and the California College of the Arts (~1955–1957).
Sachin Kathale works in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned an M.Phil. from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and has served as a teacher at Samskrita Bharati.
Sachindra Kumar Maity worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1953–1956) and held a post at Jadavpur University (attested 1965).

Sadajiro Sugiura worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Philadelphia Divinity School, holding posts at the University of Pennsylvania, Army War College, and Rikkyo University.
Saerji is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has served as an Associate Professor (attested 2010–2016) and faculty member (attested 2026) at Peking University.
Sai Susarla works in computational Indology. He has served as Dean at MIT World Peace University (attested 2019) and held a post at the Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation (attested 2025).
